summary: The frame every screen sits in: header, navigation, a named content region.
useWhen: building any full application screen rather than an embedded widget
structure: Header at the top with the brand in `brand`, primary navigation in `center` and account actions in `end`.
One <main> content region, named, holding the page's own heading as its h1.
ToastProvider mounted once around the whole shell, not per route.
Breadcrumbs, when present, sit inside <main> above the h1 — they describe where the content is, not where the chrome is.

When navigation is hierarchical or longer than a header row holds, a Sidebar replaces the NavItems in Header's `center`: Header keeps the brand and account actions, and the Sidebar sits beside <main> as the primary navigation. Below the tablet breakpoint the same Sidebar moves into a Drawer opened by Header's own toggle with `menuType="dialog"` — one copy, not two, and one menu button.

loading.must: Render the shell immediately and load only the content region. Never block the header on the page's data.
loading.why: the navigation is what a user reaches for when a page is slow; hiding it makes a slow page feel like a broken one

empty.must: A route with nothing in it still renders the shell, the heading, and a statement of what would be here.
empty.why: a blank content region with working chrome reads as a failed load

error.must: Keep the shell. Put the error inside <main> with a retry and a way back to somewhere that works.
error.why: a full-page error strands the user with no navigation, so their only option is the browser's back button

requires: `menuLabel` on Header — the mobile toggle is icon-only
a <nav> with its own accessible name wrapping the NavItems; Header supplies the banner landmark, not the navigation one
exactly one <main>, and exactly one h1 inside it
`aria-current="page"` on the NavItem for the current route — colour alone does not tell a screen-reader user where they are
with a Sidebar, `isCurrent` on the SidebarItem for the current route, and a Sidebar `label` distinct from any other nav on the page
notes: The desktop/tablet/mobile switch is a media query inside Header. Do not duplicate that decision in React state.

antiPatterns.why: toasts queued before a navigation are unmounted mid-announcement, and two live regions announce over each other

antiPatterns.dont: the page title as an h2 because the logo is an h1
antiPatterns.why: the brand is not a heading; the page's subject is

antiPatterns.dont: a Sidebar AND the same destinations as NavItems in Header
antiPatterns.why: two navigation landmarks listing the same pages double every link a screen-reader user tabs through

antiPatterns.dont: rendering a second nav for mobile
antiPatterns.why: Header moves the one copy, and two copies duplicate every link in the accessibility tree
